name: Dimmer Switch (High Wattage)

productKeyVerification.note: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) gives this category and subcategory's key to the SwitchLinc Dimmer 1200W [2476D], not to this model; that this product reports the same key is read from its sharing the identity.

verification.note: Read from the product having one load, which its group 1 controls, as on other one-load products.

steps.text: At the circuit breaker or fuse panel, turn off the circuit supplying power to the switch.
Remove the faceplate from the existing switch, then unscrew the switch and pull it out from the wall box.
Disconnect the wires from the old switch and make sure there is 1/2 inch of bare wire on the ends.
Turn the power back on.
Use a line voltage meter to identify the line, load, neutral and ground wires.
Turn the breaker off again.
Connect the switch's wires to the line, load, neutral and ground wires. Make sure all wire connectors are firmly attached and no copper is exposed except the ground wire.
With the LED bar at the left, gently place the switch into the wall box and screw it into place.
Turn power to the switch back on at the circuit breaker or fuse panel.
Use the paddle to turn the light on and off to check that the switch works.
Reinstall the faceplate.

notes: A neutral connection is required; the switch will not work without one. The switch being replaced usually has no neutral connected, but neutral wires are usually available in the back of the box.

In a virtual multi-way circuit only the primary switch is wired to the load. The secondaries connect to line, neutral and ground with their load wire capped, the black traveler is converted to a line wire and the red traveler is capped at both ends. Then link the switches to each other as a group.

verification.note: Read from the 600W Dimmer Switch 2476D Owner's Manual; no 2476DH document was found.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps, about 3 seconds.

notes: As a controller: after the switch beeps, set the responder to the state to recall (for a multi-scene device such as a KeypadLinc, tap the scene button) and press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds. The switch double-beeps and its status LED stops blinking.

As a responder: press and hold the controller's SET or scene button until it beeps or its LED blinks, use the switch to set its load to the state to recall, then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps, about 3 seconds. The status LED flashes once, then turns on solid.
For a group, such as a 2-switch circuit, link the switch as a controller of the other device and the other device as a controller of the switch.

verification.note: The Dimmer Switch 2476D Quick Start Guide (rev 01-06-2010) says to press and hold the paddle top for about 10 seconds to enter linking mode or to link as a responder; the later Dimmer Switch 2476D Owner's Manual says to press and hold the SET button for about 3 seconds. The catalog uses the owner's manual's SET button for 3 seconds.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps, about 3 seconds.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

The Insteon Developer's Guide (2009) says i1 devices don't support Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), and the catalog doesn't know the engine of every version of this product. An i2 or i2CS version takes it; ask the device with Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) first.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, adjust it to the desired state.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it beeps or its LED flashes.
After adding all responders, tap the SET button.

verification.note: Read from the Dimmer Switch 2476D Owner's Manual; no 2476DH document was found.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps, about 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button again until the switch beeps, about 3 seconds.
Press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: The switch double-beeps and its status LED stops blinking

notes: The switch stays in unlinking mode for 4 minutes.

To remove the switch as a responder: press and hold the controller's SET or scene button until it beeps or its LED blinks, do it again, then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps.

To remove several responders at once: hold the SET button until it beeps, hold it again until it beeps, then tap it (status LED double-blinks red); hold each responder's SET button until it beeps or its LED flashes, then tap the switch's SET button.

verification.note: Read from the Dimmer Switch 2476D Owner's Manual; no 2476DH document was found.

steps.text: Pull out the SET button to create an air gap.
Wait 10 seconds.
Push in the SET button and hold it. Do not let go.
When the beep stops, release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the switch double-beeps, the LEDs return to normal brightness and the load turns on

verification.note: Read from the Dimmer Switch 2476D Owner's Manual; no 2476DH document was found.

steps.text: Unlink each responder that the switch controls.
Unlink the switch from all of its controllers.
Disable or remove the switch.

notes: Otherwise the switch and its controllers keep retrying commands, causing delays in the Insteon network.

verification.note: Read from the Dimmer Switch 2476D Owner's Manual; no 2476DH document was found.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.
